_meta.purpose: Recategorises LEVEL 1 (the ceiling) from 'contract types found in the Qur'an' to 'FINANCIAL WORDS of the Qur'an'. Three tiers: (A) prohibitions & commands, (B) obligations & benevolence, (C) commerce & contract words. Every entry links down to existing terms/contracts and to its AAOIFI landing.
_meta.dating_rule: UNDATED BY RULE - the whole layer is the single undated starting block. No years anywhere in this file.
_meta.tag_policy: verse existence = verified (standard mushaf references, checkable in the app's Qur'an). Phrase gists and meaning summaries = plausible (paraphrase; the app's tafsir texts are the checkable source, hooked via tafsir_edition_ids). Standard landings = verified where the SS name/text was confirmed from ss1-ss3.txt, else plausible.
_meta.tafsir_hook_note: The app carries these tafsir editions (seen in lineage_v4 crosstags): en-tafsir-ibn-abbas, ar-tafsir-al-tabari, ar-tafsir-al-qurtubi, ar/en/ur/bn tafsir-ibn-kathir, en-tafsir-maarif-ul-quran. Each verse_ref below can open any of them - BV should link verse -> tafsir panel.
_meta.honesty_rules: Words NOT in the Qur'an are never dressed up as Qur'anic: gharar (financial sense), waqf, tawarruq, sukuk, takaful are marked origin: hadith-era / fiqh-era / modern. This is the 'origin honest' feature.
_meta.sources: Qur'an standard references; lineage_v4.json L001-L103 (existing contract anchors reused verbatim); terms.json (coverage scan); ss1-ss3.txt (SS names + SS 19 clauses verified-to-text); standards_kb.json (11 GS notes).

worked_example_qard_hasan.headline: One word's journey: Qard Hasan from 'a loan to Allah' to AAOIFI SS 19

chain.content: Six verses call giving 'a goodly loan to Allah' (2:245; 5:12; 57:11; 57:18; 64:17; 73:20). 2:282 supplies the documentation duty for all debt.

Bukhari 2068: the Prophet himself borrowed against pledged armor - borrowing is legitimate. Ibn Majah 2430 ('lending twice counts as charity once') is graded DA'EEF in the app - kept as SUPPORTING evidence only, per project rule 4.
Ibn Kathir on 57:11 and 64:17: the 'loan to Allah' as charitable spending with guaranteed manifold return.
Four-school consensus: qard is gratuitous; ANY stipulated increase is riba; repay the exact substitute.

The one word became at least SEVEN modern forms: (1) current accounts - SS 19 10/1/1 rules they ARE qard, not deposits; (2) qard hasan benevolent funds (T172); (3) Islamic microfinance (family F12); (4) ar-rahnu pawnbroking = qard + rahn combo (T171 + T016); (5) inter-bank mutual overdrafts (SS 19 preface names them); (6) hibah-on-repayment practice - voluntary excess allowed by SS 19 5/2, the basis of 'gift' returns on savings (T200) and a LIVE DISPUTE when it becomes customary; (7) benevolent side of takaful surplus lending.

AAOIFI SS 19 (Loan/Qard) - verified clauses from ss1.txt: 4/1 stipulated excess = riba in any form (quality, quantity, benefit, written or customary); 5/2 voluntary excess at repayment is permissible if not stipulated/customary; 7 no tying a sale or lease into the qard; 9/1-9/2 service charges limited to ACTUAL DIRECT costs, method set by the Shari'ah Supervisory Board, indirect costs (salaries, rent) excluded; 10/1/1 current accounts are loans.

The compliance checklist a bank running qard products faces, using our 11 GS notes: GS 1 framework (KB-GS1) - who approves the product; GS 9 compliance function (KB-GS9) - who checks the service-charge math against SS 19 9/1; GS 11 internal audit (KB-GS11) - who re-checks it. This is exactly the ceiling-to-floor story: a Qur'anic word ends as an auditable line item.
